This appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and decree dated 04.03.2011 passed in O.P.No.598 of 2011 by the learned Chairman, Motor Accident Claim Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Medak at Sangareddy (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal"), whereby the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,54,000/- with interest @ 8% per annum, for the injuries sustained by the appellant herein in a motor vehicle accident.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Medak at Sangareddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal grossly erred in failing to award any amount towards future loss of income due to disability, despite evidence from PW.2, the Orthopedic Surgeon, confirming a disability of 30-40%.

It is further contended that the compensation awarded under the heads of pain and suffering, future surgery, and loss of future amenities is meager and inadequate considering the severity of the injuries, which included open fractures of both bones of the right leg and a displaced fracture of the left humerus.

3. On the other hand, the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal has already awarded a just and reasonable compensation based on the evidence available on record.

He argued that as the appellant's work was supervisory in nature, the disability would not significantly impact his future earning capacity, and thus the order of the Tribunal requires no interference.
4. As seen from the material placed on record, the appellant sustained grievous injuries in an accident that occurred on 29.05.2011 involving a lorry bearing No.KA-39-8620.

sentences.text: Taking into consideration the nature of injuries and the disability of 30-40% sustained by the appellant, this Court finds it just to enhance the compensation under various heads.

While the Tribunal declined to award for future loss of income on the grounds that the appellant's work was supervisory, this Court is of the opinion that such a significant physical impairment necessitates a specific award for disability.
Consequently, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reassessed.
This Court awards Rs.1,00,000/- for the permanent disability sustained by the appellant and amount awarded under the head pain and suffering is enhanced from Rs.35,000/- to Rs.80,000/-.
The expenditure for future surgery is enhanced from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.40,000/-, and the loss of income during the period of treatment, rest, and recovery is enhanced from Rs.15,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
Furthermore, the award for loss of future amenities of life is enhanced from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
The amounts awarded by the Tribunal for medical expenditure totaling Rs.2,40,424/-, transportation at Rs.23,450/-, and motorcycle damages at Rs.10,000/- remain undisturbed.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,54,000/-.
5.
In the result, this appeal is partly-allowed and compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.3,54,000/- to Rs.5,54,000/-.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The remaining terms and conditions imposed by the Tribunal shall stand unaltered.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
